paper.title: MobileSteward: Integrating Multiple App-Oriented Agents with Self-Evolution to Automate Cross-App Instructions
paper.central_claim: App-oriented multi-agent framework (Steward + per-app Staff agents; Dynamic Recruitment, Assigned Execution, Adjusted Evaluation) with Memory-based Self-evolution (Staff Expertise Memory, Task Guideline Memory) achieves best results on cross-app mobile instructions (CAPBench).

gap.author_gap: Procedure-oriented/single mobile agents fail on cross-app instructions: complex task relationships, diverse app environments, error propagation and information loss; MobileAgent-v2 is a static framework without experience accumulation.
gap.checked_gap: The multi-agent decomposition gap is plausible and supported by baseline SR near 0 on CAPBench; the retained-component gap (static -> self-evolving memory) is thin: it is stated as an analogy to a steward gaining familiarity, not as a measured failure of static memory.
lineage: AppAgent (exploration/demo-generated element docs) -> MobileAgent / MobileAgent-v2 (planning/decision/reflection agents + memory unit) -> MobileSteward (app-oriented agents + evolving expertise/guideline memory)
Experience-memory neighbors named but not compared as evolving systems: MobileGPT hierarchical app memory, AutoDroid UTG memory (AutoDroid run only as a baseline)
gap.closest_adjacent: MobileAgent-v2 and AutoDroid/MobileGPT experience memories, as characterized in this paper's Related Work (original texts not in the pinned input package)
gap.residue: Cross-app tasks need scheduling and information hand-off; static per-app prompts cannot adapt to app-specific tricks.
gap.stakes: Success rate on CAPBench of baselines 0.00-0.21 vs 0.55-0.59.
gap.method_response: Per-app agents with retrievable successful-task guidelines and Steward-held app expertise; reflection and info passing between agents.
gap.remaining_gap: No evidence that the memory (not extra retries/steps/prompt structure) closes the evolving-memory gap beyond +0.05 SR; no comparison against another experience-memory scheme; deployment without trusted success signal untested.
unresolved: Whether Task Guideline Memory vs Staff Expertise Memory each carry gain
Original MobileGPT text not in pinned inputs; closest-neighbor comparison unresolved

G.reason: Opus sides with son55. The cross-app limitation is real (baselines ≤0.21 SR on CAPBench) and MobileAgent-v2 is run, but this domain's G asks what fixed non-weight object becomes adaptive and how it differs from same-class memory neighbours: the self-evolution gap is an analogy (opus:O01), and the app-specific experience memories of MobileGPT/AutoDroid are dismissed in one sentence without comparison (opus:O02). Real limitation with incomplete neighbour comparison = anchor 2; sol's 3 credits the multi-agent gap but not the memory residual.

M.reason: Opus sides with sol. Each named bottleneck (task relations, app diversity, error propagation) maps to a module whose removal is tested, and the decomposition makes a distinguishing prediction (smaller degradation as app count grows) that is checked (opus:O03). Below 4 because the retention mechanism's key assumption (self-judged success is a reliable write gate) is unexamined and the M_E update rule is unspecified; son55's points on the update rule are charged under X (2), not twice.

X.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. Algorithm 1 gives the write/read chain (Extract→Update, BM25 top-3 read, M_E in Schedule), but M_G is append-only (opus:O05), M_E admission is one LLM decision, no versioning/rollback/retirement, prompts absent.

E.measurement.reason: Opus sides with son55. Success Rate is defined only as 'whether the instruction is completed' with no stated adjudicator (human, rule or LLM); App Rate is satisfiable by opening the labelled apps; CAPBench is GPT-4-generated from authors' templates; the full-model ablation row contradicts Table 2 (opus:O04). The headline metric's validator is unverifiable, which is below the anchor-2 'relevant results with gaps'.

E.causality.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. Evolution-off and module ablations exist (Table 3), but M_E and M_G are removed jointly, one run, baselines get 80 steps vs 20×3 per sub-task and different base models, and no alternative memory scheme is compared.

E.holdout.reason: Both seats 1; re-checked and kept. Build/test instructions are disjoint, but memories keep updating on the test stream (index_experience F3 / H00 step 4 failure mode), build and test items are instantiated from one template pool with no overlap audit, and the 50-task online-user check measures the system, not the frozen store.

E.statistics.reason: Both seats 1 (A2 ladder): sample sizes (150 test, 50 SAP, 100 MobileAgentBench, 50 online) and degradations are reported, but one run, no intervals; the +0.05 SR memory effect is ~7-8 tasks.

E.cost.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. Actions/task and tokens/action vs MobileAgent-v2 are reported (Table 6); the ~350-instruction build phase, Extract/Update/Evaluate calls and the unequal step budget are not costed.

resolutions.reason: EVIDENCE.md 'retained' = a retained change improves later tasks, preferably on independent held-out tasks. The store is built on non-test instructions and the evolution-off contrast is measured on the disjoint 150-task split (0.55 vs 0.50). Online test-time updates and template siblings weaken holdout (E.holdout=1) but do not turn this into a selection-set-only result; the test set never selects what is kept.

The central contribution (object-oriented split, DAG scheduling, app-specialist delegation, three of four contributions) is a decomposition move; memory conditioning is one module. sol's reason for rejecting C25 (no sound solver) is correct and retained at sub level, not at parent level.
Both parents apply with sub null; sol's conditioning match is kept as the supporting entry.

H01 is defined by an editing policy over existing entries (update/merge/delete/forget). MobileSteward has only a write/no-write decision for M_E and append-only M_G (opus:O05); son55's own check found no consolidation. H00 (extract lessons from own outcomes and append) fits better, at medium-low fit (successes only, no contrast).
